answer: Cross-Epoch Drift Lock. Each identity commits a behavioural fingerprint per epoch; the next epoch must match it within a fixed tolerance on task mix, timing, and counterparties. Mismatch beyond tolerance freezes the identity until it re-earns continuity across a tundra-like cold period of zero rewards. An attacker must run every clone through that same costly consistency track, like tending a cedar slowly rather than cloning it, so each fake identity burns an inlet of real compute and time before it can act.
